text: 6 Killed in Ukrainian Drone Strikes Across Russia and Crimea Sep. 7, 2026 An apartment building in Perm after a Ukrainian drone strike. @exilenova_plus / Telegram At least six people were killed in a wave of Ukrainian drone attacks targeting Russia’s Belgorod and Perm regions and annexed Crimea overnight, officials said Monday. A man and woman were killed when a drone struck their car in the Belgorod region near the border with Ukraine, according to the local emergency headquarters. On Monday morning, officials in Belgorod said a man was killed in a separate drone attack in the border town of Grayvoron. In the Perm region, 1,300 kilometers (800 miles) east of Ukraine, one person was killed and four were injured after a drone hit an apartment building, Governor Dmitry Mahonin said . Unverified reports said smoke was seen rising over an industrial area in Perm that houses at least two defense facilities, including a gunpowder plant and a rocket engine manufacturing facility. Meanwhile, in annexed Crimea, a 15-year-old girl and a man were killed in an overnight attack in the port city of Sevastopol. title: Avalanche in Kabardino-Balkaria Kills 11 Climbers
text: Avalanche in Kabardino-Balkaria Kills 11 Climbers By Reuters Sep. 7, 2026 Russian emergency personnel. Emergency Situations Ministry At least 11 people were killed and six others injured after an avalanche struck a group of climbers in Russia 's Kabardino-Balkaria region in the North Caucasus, local emergency services said. The avalanche swept down Mount Mizhirgi, one of the highest peaks in Russia 's North Caucasus, at around 5 p.m. local time on Sunday, hitting a group of 33 climbers. As of 9 a.m. local time on Monday, 10 climbers had made their own way down the mountain, while the fate of six others remained unknown, emergency services said. More than 50 emergency workers were involved in the search and rescue operation, but efforts were being hampered by difficult terrain and a high risk of further avalanches, they said. text: «Тень Путина над Европой» — на Западе испугались победы «АдГ» в Саксонии-Анхальт Накануне правая немецкая партия «АдГ» победила с рекордным результатом в 43,8% на выборах в парламент федеральной земли Саксония-Анхальт. Правящий Христианско-демократический союз (ХДС) Мерца, в свою очередь, получил рекордно низкие 17,2% голосов. В истеблишменте ФРГ и среди западных либералов такой результат уже вызвал панику. В частности, Мерц заявил, что Германия столкнулась «с тектоническим сдвигом» в партийной системе после победы «АдГ». Целью победившей партии, по мнению канцлера, является полное уничтожение «ХДС». Мерц при этом намекнул на возможность запрета партии, отметив, что в Германии есть инструменты «для защиты конституционного строя от праворадикального правительства». Тем временем Bloomberg уже выпустил статью с заголовком «Тень Путина над Европой растет на фоне победы немецких ультраправых». В разговоре с Readovka политолог и бывший советник правительства ФРГ Александр Рар заявил, что победа «АдГ» в Саксонии-Анхальт — это личное поражение Мерца. text: Ломоносова и Державина исключили из программы русских школ в Литве С нового учебного года произведения Михаила Ломоносова и Гавриила Державина убрали из программы родного языка и литературы для девятиклассников русского национального меньшинства, сообщает LRT. Ранее премьер Литвы Миндаугас Синкявичюс предложил пересмотреть список русских классиков в школьной программе. По его словам, Ломоносов не должен использоваться для воспитания «патриотизма и гражданственности», поскольку прославлял войны Российской империи. Вместо русских классиков премьер предложил изучать украинского поэта Тараса Шевченко. Однако его произведения в программу пока не добавили. text: Редкого белого сокола продали в Абу-Даби за рекордные 2,1 млн дирхамов Белый кречет Gyr Pure Ultra White ушел с аукциона в столице ОАЭ за 2,1 млн дирхамов (~₽49 млн). Это новый мировой рекорд: предыдущий был установлен в 2021 году в Эр-Рияде, где за белого кречета заплатили $467 тыс (~₽40,4 млн). Торги прошли в рамках выставки охоты, рыболовства и коневодства ADIHEX. Высокая цена на таких птиц объясняется не только редким окрасом: соколов ценят за происхождение, физические данные и охотничьи качества. В аукционе участвовали 55 местных и зарубежных заводчиков. Для ОАЭ сокол — не просто дорогая птица, а национальный символ и часть многовековой традиции . Соколиная охота входит в список нематериального культурного наследия ЮНЕСКО, а для самих птиц в стране работают специализированные больницы и предусмотрена медицинская страховка. 🎉 Подписывайся на Readovka в МАКС

text: Правительство поручило проверить эффективность форумов, проводимых за счет федерального и региональных бюджетов Соответствующее поручение Минэкономразвитию совместно с Минфином дал премьер-министр Михаил Мишустин. До 1 декабря 2026 года ведомства должны оценить эффективность таких мероприятий и представить правительству предложения по оптимизации их проведения. Политолог Евгений Минченко в разговоре с Readovka отметил, что на фоне экономии бюджета вопрос о том, нужно ли России такое количество форумов, вполне закономерен. Обычно об их эффективности судят по суммам подписанных соглашений, однако эксперт считает такой показатель далеко не самым точным. «Как правило, на форум приезжают с уже готовыми соглашениями. Поэтому говорить о том, что „ну вот, видите, мы тут провели форум, зато там на офигелиард денег подписали соглашений“… Ну вопрос: а не было бы форума, соглашений, что ли, не было бы? Или они все-таки все равно были бы?» — прокомментировал Минченко. Лексика спикера сохранена. При этом эксперт подчеркнул, что сам относится к форумам положительно. По его словам, их главная ценность заключается в горизонтальной коммуникации: на одной площадке одновременно встречаются губернаторы
author: Readovka

text: Суд ЕС отказал Литве в произвольной трактовке санкций против России Одной связи компании с Россией недостаточно, чтобы распространять на нее европейские санкции, постановил Суд ЕС. Поводом стало дело литовской энергетической компании Inter Rao Lietuva, активы которой местные власти заморозили в 2022 году. Сама компания под санкциями ЕС не находилась. Однако литовские власти решили, что она косвенно подконтрольна российским властям: Inter Rao Lietuva через финскую компанию была связана с российской «Интер РАО», среди крупнейших акционеров которой есть подконтрольные государству структуры. На этом основании в Вильнюсе пришли к выводу, что президент России якобы может фактически контролировать компанию, а значит, на нее можно распространить ограничения. Суд ЕС счел такую логику недостаточной. Для заморозки активов необходимо доказать контроль конкретного подсанкционного лица над компанией объективными и достаточно вескими доказательствами . Сам по себе характер российской политической системы или связь владельцев компании с государством таким доказательством не являются. Теперь дело вернется в Верховный административный суд Литвы, который должен рассмотреть спор с учетом позиции Суда
author: Readovka

title: Australia politics live: John Howard warns about limiting immigration; Barnaby Joyce says super plan to have ‘minute’ inflationary effect
text: 16.42 EDT John Howard says blocking immigration from certain countries won't stop terrorism Sarah Basford Canales The former prime minister John Howard has warned political parties against banning migration from certain countries as the debate over Australia’s immigration settings continues . The 87-year-old was in Canberra last night for an hour-long chat with Australian National University national security professor Rory Medcalf before the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks in the US. The discussion began with last year’s alleged terrorist attack in Bondi, before turning to whether immigration settings can prevent potential terrorists from entering the country. Howard said the “law of averages” meant some people with nefarious intentions could enter the country but he did not believe the “evidence is overwhelming”. He continued: But I think the mood is overwhelming that we have to try very hard to stop terrorism creeping in under the cover of immigration, and you can’t do it by just stopping immigration, and it’s very hard to do it by stopping categories of immigration. text: Sarah Jones tells MPs ‘those responsible should expect to face the consequences’ Healey says Andy Burnham set out in his statement to MPs last week what he thought had gone wrong The fundamentals of our economy [were] hollowed out through a series of past policy decisions, political power was centralised, weakening the relationships between the people, the businesses and the institutions who can make things happen beyond Whitehall. The economic enablers were privatised and outsourced, leaving accountability to a thicket of arm’s length bodies and regulators, too often without the predictability or the pace that underpins a thriving market economy. And our country was deindustrialised as the cost to make anything, to build anything here soared, and our dependence on unreliable sources grew, including in areas critical to our national security and sovereignty. Let me be clear, I recognise that the costs of business, its energy bills, regulation, burdens, planning constraints, labour costs, have grown since Covid and I want to draw the line. text: Уничтожены три оперативные ячейки террористической группировки на юго-востоке Ирана Благодаря божественной милости героические сотрудники Министерства разведки Ирана на основе данных разведки и сообщений граждан сумели уничтожить три организованные оперативные ячейки террористических группировок такфиритского толка, связанных с американо-сионистским врагом, в момент их проникновения на территорию страны, ещё до совершения каких-либо диверсионных или террористических действий. Трое террористов были ликвидированы в ходе столкновения с силами безопасности, ещё девять прибывших из-за рубежа террористов были задержаны. Задержанные наёмники, прошедшие за пределами страны военную подготовку, обучение минированию и совершению террористических убийств и пытавшиеся тайно проникнуть в Иран, намеревались дестабилизировать обстановку в южных районах провинции и нанести удар по спокойствию и общественной безопасности этих территорий. У задержанных террористов было обнаружено и изъято значительное количество оружия и боеприпасов. Кроме того, в ходе продолжающихся целенаправленных разведывательных операций против преступных банд и группировок силы безопасности Ирана обнаружили и изъяли склад лёгко

title: Ukraine’s prosecutor general submits resignation after senior subordinate is accused of shielding fraudulent call centers
text: Ukraine’s prosecutor general submits resignation after senior subordinate is accused of shielding fraudulent call centers September 7, 2026, 11:19 pm Source: Ruslan Kravchenko Ukraine’s Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko said on Telegram that he had submitted his resignation. “This was a deliberate political decision. I don’t want the role of prosecutor general used as a tool in a political conflict. My position on the allegations has not changed,” Kravchenko said. Last week, Ukraine’s National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) searched the Prosecutor General’s Office. Serhiy Kropyva, deputy head of the office’s International Cooperation Department, was accused of running a network that “provided cover for” fraudulent call centers. He was detained. Kravchenko had previously said he did not plan to resign over Kropyva’s detention: “I don’t feel I should do that. There’s a procedure: the Verkhovna Rada can vote, and the president can initiate the resignation. If they do so, I will, of course, comply.” Kravchenko had served as Ukraine’s prosecutor general since June 2025. title: Putin ‘does not want to upset’ Trump and is ‘ready to discuss’ peace ideas, Zelensky says
text: Putin ‘does not want to upset’ Trump and is ‘ready to discuss’ peace ideas, Zelensky says September 7, 2026, 11:11 pm Source: Axios U.S. presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner discussed potential de-escalation steps with Moscow and Kyiv ahead of and during the winter, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told Axios . Zelensky said one of Witkoff and Kushner’s goals was to revive stalled peace talks between Russia and Ukraine. Another was to try to make the coming winter different from previous ones, when Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure intensified the conflict. Zelensky said he is convinced that, as in previous years, Russia plans to launch major attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure this fall and winter. He also said, however, that Russian President Vladimir Putin “doesn’t want … to upset him,” referring to U.S. President Donald Trump, and is “ready to discuss” ideas for moving negotiations forward. Witkoff and Kushner visited Moscow on September 5 and Kyiv on September 6. It was their first visit to the Ukrainian capital since the war began. title: Kyiv air raid alerts at record high as Russia launches round-the-clock strikes
text: Kyiv air raid alerts at record high as Russia launches round-the-clock strikes Figure caption, Watch: Kyiv residents on living under daily attacks by Russia By James Landale ,Â Diplomatic correspondent ,Â Reporting from Kyiv Â and Â Christine Jeavans ,Â Senior data journalist Published 7 September 2026, 08:03 BST Kyiv is suffering more daily air raid alerts than at any time since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, according to BBC Verify analysis of government figures. Most air attacks used to come at night but Russia's new tactic of striking Ukraine's capital during the day is causing huge disruption to schools and businesses. The round the clock attacks have forced people to head for shelter as many as 13 times a day, with air raid alerts lasting from a few minutes to nearly four and a half hours. Residents in Kyiv are struggling to adapt to this new reality, adding to existing stress and anxiety. The alerts force pupils to leave their classrooms and workers their offices and leave commuters struggling to get home as overland trains stop. text: ‼️ 🇷🇺 🏴‍☠️ Яркий финал «Зарницы 2.0» вызывает скрежет зубовный у предателей и врагов России ▪️ Манёвры вызвали ненависть у беглых либералов и внутренних врагов, причитающих о «милитаризации детского сознания». Впрочем, их с той же силой бесит и Крестный ход, пишет военкор и депутат Андрей Медведев. ▪️ Однако «Зарница» всегда была не про войну, несмотря на танки, взрывы, ББМ, слаженную работу в связках, штурмы окопов и наложение жгутов. ▪️ Главное, что усвоят дети и что будет работать на них всю жизнь, — это командный дух и наставники-фронтовики. Те самые значимые взрослые, на которых хочется равняться. Дети запомнят не количество выстрелов, а радость преодоления невозможного и осознание того, что ты старался и сделал всё возможное, даже если не победил. ▪️ В памяти останутся вечерние разговоры у костра, верные друзья, с которыми пройден весь путь, и, возможно, первая любовь, которая останется навсегда. ▪️ Как и великая культура, эта игра укрепляет дух и даёт важнейшие смыслы: «я смогу, когда надо, не подведу команду и не забуду, что моя Родина — великая страна». ▪️ Большинство участников не станут военными, но полученные в полях навыки пригодятся в любом деле: в бизнесе, госуправле

title: Australia politics live: Joyce says One Nation ‘shouldn’t have to model’ super plan; Chaney condemns Labor ‘park barrelling’ allegations
text: 17.57 EDT ‘We shouldn’t have to model’ super changes, Joyce says Barnaby Joyce is using every which way he can to say that One Nation shouldn’t have to model the impact of One Nation’s policy that would allow an individual to divert 3% of their superannuation to pay their rent or mortgage. After a pretty heated exchange on 7.30 last night, Joyce is back on the ABC speaking to RN Breakfast, and there’s once again a lot of back and forth. He says having to model what happens to someone getting access to their own money is “conceptualised by socialism”. Is there an implication beyond it being their money? Do you model the money you get paid at the end of the week? Do you have to model that money before you get paid? Or do you believe you have an entitlement to your own money? … We shouldn’t have to model you getting your own money. When host Sally Sara then asks whether economists have backed the policy, Joyce ridicules the suggestion. Now we have to get economists to decide whether you get access to your own money … now we’ve got another group of people that apparently have to give approval for you to get your money. I mean, who else do you want to go to? Your local priest, Buddhist

Most air attacks used to come at night but Russia's new tactic of striking Ukraine's capital during the day is causing huge disruption to schools and businesses. The round the clock attacks have forced people to head for shelter as many as 13 times a day, with air raid alerts lasting from a few minutes to nearly four and a half hours. Residents in Kyiv are struggling to adapt to this new reality, adding to existing stress and anxiety. title: Avalanche in Kabardino-Balkaria Kills 11 Climbers
text: Avalanche in Kabardino-Balkaria Kills 11 Climbers By Reuters Sep. 7, 2026 Russian emergency personnel. Emergency Situations Ministry At least 11 people were killed and six others injured after an avalanche struck a group of climbers in Russia 's Kabardino-Balkaria region in the North Caucasus, local emergency services said. The avalanche swept down Mount Mizhirgi, one of the highest peaks in Russia 's North Caucasus, at around 5 p.m. local time on Sunday, hitting a group of 33 climbers. As of 9 a.m. local time on Monday, 10 climbers had made their own way down the mountain, while the fate of six others remained unknown, emergency services said. More than 50 emergency workers were involved in the search and rescue operation, but efforts were being hampered by difficult terrain and a high risk of further avalanches, they said. The AfD’s breakthrough in Saxony-Anhalt should be understood, according to Sylvie Bermann, as part of a wider transformation of European politics rather than as an isolated German electoral shock. title: Russia Orders Closures of German Consulate and Cultural Centers in Tit-for-Tat Move
text: Russia Orders Closures of German Consulate and Cultural Centers in Tit-for-Tat Move Sep. 7, 2026 The German Consulate General in St. Petersburg. GAlexandrova (CC BY-SA 4.0) Russia’s Foreign Ministry said Monday it was shuttering the German consulate in St. Petersburg and German cultural centers across the country. The closures were announced in retaliation for Germany’s decision last week to close the Russian consulate in Bonn and a Russian cultural center in Berlin after its government blamed Moscow for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month. Moscow gave diplomats and employees at the German Consulate General in St. Petersburg until Sept. 18 to cease operations and leave Russia. title: Moscow Police General and Gas Station Executives Arrested in Fuel Theft Scheme
text: Moscow Police General and Gas Station Executives Arrested in Fuel Theft Scheme Sep. 7, 2026 Alexander Avilov / Moskva News Agency Law enforcement authorities in the Moscow region have arrested a police general, two senior officers and several corporate executives at a local gas station network accused of stealing fuel designated for police vehicles, Russia’s Interior Ministry said Monday. Major General Sergei Malkov, who managed logistics as deputy head of the Moscow region ’s Interior Ministry branch, allegedly oversaw the criminal scheme alongside Igor Martyshov, board chairman of EuroTrans, a major gas station operator. Malkov and two of his subordinates, Colonel Alexei Suyarov and Lieutenant Colonel Anna Levina, were fired from the Interior Ministry following their arrests. Investigators have asked a judge to place them in pre-trial detention. Interior Ministry spokeswoman Irina Volk said three other EuroTrans executives have been placed in pre-trial detention. All seven individuals face charges of large-scale embezzlement, which carry a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison. The arrests come after antitrust authorities in June accused EuroTrans, which operates 57 gas stations

title: Communist Bondarenko Barred From Running in State Duma Elections
text: Communist Bondarenko Barred From Running in State Duma Elections Sep. 7, 2026 Nikolai Bondarenko. kprf.ru The Central Election Commission on Monday barred Communist Party candidate Nikolai Bondarenko from running in Russia’s upcoming parliamentary elections following his recent conviction for displaying “extremist” symbols. Bondarenko, a former Saratov regional lawmaker and popular YouTuber with more than 2 million subscribers, was detained and fined last month over an old social media post featuring a photo of the late opposition activist Alexei Navalny. His defense team argued that the account that made the post does not belong to Bondarenko. A judge rejected an appeal against the ruling and fine last week. On Monday, election officials, citing the “extremism” charge, voted to remove Bondarenko from the ballot in this month’s State Duma elections. Russian election laws prohibit anyone convicted of an “extremism” offense from running for office for a year. In a statement, the Communist Party accused officials of blocking Bondarenko’s election bid because they are “afraid.” news Moscow Police Detain Yabloko Candidates Running in State Duma Elections Read more Bondarenko rose to nat

title: Russia and North Korea Open First Road Bridge Across Shared Border
text: Russia and North Korea Open First Road Bridge Across Shared Border Sep. 7, 2026 North Korean trucks drive along the newly inaugurated Novichenko bridge. @kozhemiakoofficial / Telegram Russia and North Korea opened the first road bridge linking the two countries on Monday, coming after months of construction delays. Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin and North Korean Premier Pak Thae Song presided over a ceremony via video link to mark the official launch of traffic along th e two-lane bridge, which stretches one kilometer (0.6 miles) over the Tumen River. Mishustin hailed bilateral relations as being at an “unprecedentedly high level of comprehensive strategic partnership,” adding that the bridge, which cost 9 billion rubles ($104 million), would boost trade and tourism. A rail bridge, built in the 1950s, already connects the two countries. news Moscow Is Touting North Korea as a New Tourism Hotspot. Few Russians Are Making the Trip. Read more The new road bridge is named after Yakov Novichenko, a Soviet officer who saved North Korean founder Kim Il Sung by shielding him from a grenade explosion in Pyongyang in 1946. title: 6 Killed in Ukrainian Drone Strikes Across Russia and Crimea
text: 6 Killed in Ukrainian Drone Strikes Across Russia and Crimea Sep. 7, 2026 An apartment building in Perm after a Ukrainian drone strike. @exilenova_plus / Telegram At least six people were killed in a wave of Ukrainian drone attacks targeting Russia’s Belgorod and Perm regions and annexed Crimea overnight, officials said Monday. A man and woman were killed when a drone struck their car in the Belgorod region near the border with Ukraine, according to the local emergency headquarters. On Monday morning, officials in Belgorod said a man was killed in a separate drone attack in the border town of Grayvoron. In the Perm region, 1,300 kilometers (800 miles) east of Ukraine, one person was killed and four were injured after a drone hit an apartment building, Governor Dmitry Mahonin said . Unverified reports said smoke was seen rising over an industrial area in Perm that houses at least two defense facilities, including a gunpowder plant and a rocket engine manufacturing facility. Meanwhile, in annexed Crimea, a 15-year-old girl and a man were killed in an overnight attack in the port city of Sevastopol. title: Avalanche in Kabardino-Balkaria Kills 11 Climbers
text: Avalanche in Kabardino-Balkaria Kills 11 Climbers By Reuters Sep. 7, 2026 Russian emergency personnel. Emergency Situations Ministry At least 11 people were killed and six others injured after an avalanche struck a group of climbers in Russia 's Kabardino-Balkaria region in the North Caucasus, local emergency services said. The avalanche swept down Mount Mizhirgi, one of the highest peaks in Russia 's North Caucasus, at around 5 p.m. local time on Sunday, hitting a group of 33 climbers. As of 9 a.m. local time on Monday, 10 climbers had made their own way down the mountain, while the fate of six others remained unknown, emergency services said. More than 50 emergency workers were involved in the search and rescue operation, but efforts were being hampered by difficult terrain and a high risk of further avalanches, they said. title: Kyiv air raid alerts at record high as Russia launches round-the-clock strikes
text: Kyiv air raid alerts at record high as Russia launches round-the-clock strikes Figure caption, Watch: Kyiv residents on living under daily attacks by Russia By James Landale ,Â Diplomatic correspondent ,Â Reporting from Kyiv Â and Â Christine Jeavans ,Â Senior data journalist Published 7 September 2026 Kyiv is suffering more daily air raid alerts than at any time since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, according to BBC Verify analysis of government figures. Most air attacks used to come at night but Russia's new tactic of striking Ukraine's capital during the day is causing huge disruption to schools and businesses. The round the clock attacks have forced people to head for shelter as many as 13 times a day, with air raid alerts lasting from a few minutes to nearly four and a half hours. Residents in Kyiv are struggling to adapt to this new reality, adding to existing stress and anxiety. The alerts force pupils to leave their classrooms and workers their offices and leave commuters struggling to get home as overland trains stop. text: Avalanche in Kabardino-Balkaria Kills 11 Climbers By Reuters Sep. 7, 2026 Russian emergency personnel. Emergency Situations Ministry At least 11 people were killed and six others injured after an avalanche struck a group of climbers in Russia 's Kabardino-Balkaria region in the North Caucasus, local emergency services said. The avalanche swept down Mount Mizhirgi, one of the highest peaks in Russia 's North Caucasus, at around 5 p.m. local time on Sunday, hitting a group of 33 climbers. As of 9 a.m. local time on Monday, 10 climbers had made their own way down the mountain, while the fate of six others remained unknown, emergency services said. More than 50 emergency workers were involved in the search and rescue operation, but efforts were being hampered by difficult terrain and a high risk of further avalanches, they said. title: Yelena Morgunova, wife of performance artist Pavel Krisevich, was due to be released from jail when a Russian court sentenced her to 14 more days over an alleged refusal to take a drug test
text: A magistrate in Russia’s Ryazan region sentenced Yelena Morgunova, the wife of performance artist Pavel Krisevich, to 14 days of administrative detention on a charge of refusing a drug test, the Slovo Zashchite project said . Morgunova was due to be released on September 7 after serving an earlier 10-day detention sentence. According to Morgunova, before her scheduled release from the detention center, she was taken to a police detective’s office. The officer said her pupils were dilated and asked her to take a drug test. Morgunova said she wanted to wait for her lawyer first. The officer treated that as a refusal to be tested. “What really bothers me is that they had just brought her out of the detention center — and immediately into a detective’s office. We asked the court to summon the witnesses who observed the procedure and the detective. The court initially granted our request, then couldn’t reach anyone and ultimately said it would proceed without them. In other words, the court acknowledged that their testimony was important but did not wait for the witnesses to appear,” Morgunova’s lawyer, Leonid Solovyov, said. title: Ukraine’s prosecutor general submits resignation after senior subordinate is accused of shielding fraudulent call centers
text: Ukraine’s Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko said on Telegram that he had submitted his resignation. “This was a deliberate political decision. I don’t want the role of prosecutor general used as a tool in a political conflict. My position on the allegations has not changed,” Kravchenko said. Last week, Ukraine’s National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) searched the Prosecutor General’s Office. Serhiy Kropyva, deputy head of the office’s International Cooperation Department, was accused of running a network that “provided cover for” fraudulent call centers. He was detained. Kravchenko had previously said he did not plan to resign over Kropyva’s detention: “I don’t feel I should do that. There’s a procedure: the Verkhovna Rada can vote, and the president can initiate the resignation. If they do so, I will, of course, comply.” Kravchenko had served as Ukraine’s prosecutor general since June 2025. title: Kyiv air raid alerts at record high as Russia launches round-the-clock strikes
text: Kyiv air raid alerts at record high as Russia launches round-the-clock strikes Figure caption, Watch: Kyiv residents on living under daily attacks by Russia By James Landale ,Â Diplomatic correspondent ,Â Reporting from Kyiv Â and Â Christine Jeavans ,Â Senior data journalist Published 7 September 2026 Kyiv is suffering more daily air raid alerts than at any time since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, according to BBC Verify analysis of government figures. Most air attacks used to come at night but Russia's new tactic of striking Ukraine's capital during the day is causing huge disruption to schools and businesses. The round the clock attacks have forced people to head for shelter as many as 13 times a day, with air raid alerts lasting from a few minutes to nearly four and a half hours. Residents in Kyiv are struggling to adapt to this new reality, adding to existing stress and anxiety. The alerts force pupils to leave their classrooms and workers their offices and leave commuters struggling to get home as overland trains stop. text: Advertising Thousands of mourners gather in Belgrade for war criminal Mladic's funeral Europe Thousands of mourners on Monday gathered at a church in Belgrade for the funeral of Ratko Mladic, who died in The Hague, Netherlands, on August 27 while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity.
